input: hey, 3 of my uni friends are visiting japan for there first time and i want to take them to a themed café for brunch this saturday, 4 of us, table from 11:00 for about 90 min. somewhere central, max ~30 min by train from shibuya, that we can reserve ahead. needs real brunch food not just a drink. i want something really unique you can only do in japan, where you're right up close with the theme instead of just looking at decor, super cute and photogenic so they post about it all week. the famous tokyo café thing tourists always rave about. budget around ¥3,500-5,000 each. can you book it?

experiences.name: Omotesando Sunday Table
experiences.description: Light-filled, minimalist brunch spot 3 minutes from Omotesando Station, with a table for 4 held at 11:00. Avocado and tomato sourdough toast, granola bowls with soy yogurt and single-origin pour-over coffee from the house roaster.

experiences.name: Mori no Hoshi Owl Brunch
experiences.description: Brunch among around 20 owls of several species, including nocturnal barn owls and scops owls, which are tethered by leg jesses to open perches in the lit dining room from 11:00 to 20:00. Guests stroke the owls and hold one on a leather glove for photos during the meal. 5 minutes from Harajuku Station; 90 minutes with one brunch plate and one drink each: avocado-tofu toast, kabocha soup, fruit sando with soy cream, matcha latte. Photography allowed; lockers for bags; groups of 4 reservable.

experiences.name: Hikari Teien Digital Brunch
experiences.description: Digital-art brunch where seasonal gardens, flowers and forest creatures bloom inside your bowl and across the table as you eat. Draw your own creature at a tablet station and watch it join the projected scene. All creatures are projected digital animations drawn by guests or artists; the café keeps no live animals on the premises. 4 minutes from Shibuya Station; bookable 90-minute timed entry with one brunch set and one drink: matcha rice porridge, vegetable tempura onigiri, yuzu fruit salad and matcha latte. Drawing tablets and souvenir cards included.

experiences.name: Uji Hanare Tea House – Matcha Ceremony for Four
experiences.description: A 45-minute guided matcha tea ceremony in English at 11:00 for a group of 4, held in a quiet tatami room near Sensō-ji. Guests whisk their own matcha and taste seasonal wagashi made from sweet bean paste and rice flour.

experiences.name: Fukurou Garden Kitchen – Owl & Hawk Falconry Brunch
experiences.description: Falconry-themed brunch café where owls and a few small hawks are tethered by leg jesses to perches along the counter and between the tables during opening hours. Staff carry a bird to each table so guests can touch it and hold it for photos while they eat. 7 minutes from Kichijoji Station, about 20 min from Shibuya on the Keio Inokashira Line; 90-minute table; rice bowls with grilled vegetables, miso soup and a hojicha parfait; group reservations up to 6.

experiences.name: Yoru no Mori Café – Projection Owl Forest Brunch
experiences.description: Immersive night-forest brunch café where projection-mapped owls glide across the walls, land on your table and react when you touch its surface. The owls are projected digital animations that respond to touch; the café keeps no live animals on the premises. 6 minutes from Harajuku Station; 90-minute session with one brunch plate and one drink each: owl-face onigiri plate, kabocha soup, avocado-tofu toast and owl latte art. Photography allowed; groups of 4 reservable for Saturday mornings.

experiences.name: Shinjuku Parfait Lab
experiences.description: Dessert café 2 minutes from Shinjuku-sanchome Station, known for towering seasonal fruit parfaits layered in tall glasses and built with Yamanashi peaches, Shizuoka melon and soy whipped cream. Reservable tables with a 60-minute limit.
